title: The Marfa Mystery Lights
author: Jon Hanson (Flickr: exaudio)
publisher: Flickr; cropped copy on Wikimedia Commons used on Wikipedia
image_url: Commons derivative: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:The_Marfa_Mystery_Lights_(3525821502)_(cropped).jpg (seen in search results, page not fetchable)
taken_from: Viewing area ('official viewing platform east of Marfa')
camera: Canon EOS 40D, 17 mm, f/2.8, 5 s, ISO 1600
skyline_or_landmarks: unknown from text; 17 mm wide-angle with stars ('stars' tag), so skyline likely in frame
analysability: high - CC BY, viewing area, exact EXIF time, wide field, stars available for astrometric pointing
notes: Best openly licensed candidate. HandWiki says Wikipedia's lead image is 'Marfa_Mystery_Light_(cropped_twice).jpg', captioned 'A Marfa light (center) seen from the official viewing platform'. That is probably a further crop of this photo, but I couldn't confirm it. Use the uncropped Flickr original.

title: Marfa Lights with the Milky Way 1508152208-DSC00577
author: Rob Pettengill
date_taken: 2015-08-15 local (EXIF 2015-08-16 03:08:08; the filename's 1508152208 suggests the camera was set to UTC, i.e. 22:08 CDT)
taken_from: Viewing area, US 90 east of Marfa
direction: toward the Milky Way, so roughly S/SSW in mid-August evening (inferred, not stated)
camera: Sony NEX-5N, 20 s, ISO 3200, lens not recorded
skyline_or_landmarks: horizon in frame; caption says 'triangle of lights at horizon in the center'
claim: Marfa lights (triangle of lights on the horizon)
analysability: high - viewing area, recoverable time, stars for plate-solving, horizon visible
notes: The NC-ND licence limits republishing derivative overlays. Ask the author for permission.

title: Marfa Lights 1
author: Nicolas Henderson (TexasExplorer98 / texasbackroads)
publisher: Flickr; reused by Vice (2017-05-09) as 'A tourist photo of one of the lights' and by texashillcountry.com (2017)
time: caption says ~21:15; EXIF says 08:42:19, so the camera clock is wrong by ~12.5 h
taken_from: Probably the viewing area (same session as his 'Marfa Lights Observation Center' photo); not stated explicitly
camera: Canon EOS Rebel T2i, 55 mm, f/5.6, 1/6 s, ISO 3200
skyline_or_landmarks: unknown; at 21:15 in late July there is residual twilight, so a skyline is possible
claim: Marfa lights seen at dusk; 'dancing around and even changing colors' later that night
analysability: medium-high - open licence, twilight skyline likely; the time has to come from the caption
notes: A companion frame follows.

title: Marfa Lights 2
author: Nicolas Henderson
camera: Canon T2i, 55 mm, f/5.6, 1/4 s, ISO 3200
analysability: medium-high - pair with -a; the 97 s gap between frames lets you check motion against US-67 speeds

title: Marfa Lights
author: David Barclay (Ranger 1)
camera: Canon EOS 30D, 200 mm, f/6.3, 30 s, ISO 200
skyline_or_landmarks: Yes - 'The red light is a radio tower'
claim: 'The two horizontal lights are the mystery lights'
analysability: high - exact time with UTC offset, known tower as an anchor, 200 mm focal length gives fine plate scale, horizontal streaks during 30 s let you test vehicle speed
notes: Enhanced in Photoshop. Ask for the original.

title: Marfa Mystery Lights
author: DBC (dbcnwa)
camera: Canon Digital Rebel XT, 35 mm, f/4.5, 30 s, ISO 100
claim: Lights 'appeared to move across the sky'; left and right patterns indicate independent movement
analysability: medium-high - full EXIF, trails in a 30 s exposure; needs the location confirmed
notes: Taken the night after the 2005-06-02/03 EBLO event in Stephan et al. 2011. The author notes possible mirror-slap blur.

title: A Marfa Light
author: Heather Klebs (heatharcadia)
direction: SOUTHEAST ('a faint glow to the southeast')
camera: Pentax K-50, 200 mm manual K/M lens, 30 s, ISO 3200
claim: A Marfa light that brightened, dimmed and brightened during the exposure
analysability: medium - good EXIF, but SE is outside the US-67 sector, so check other roads, ranch lights and Alpine-area sources
notes: Good test of the model beyond US-67.

title: Day 5: The Marfa Lights

title: Bunnell ML series, 3 sequential photos
author: James Bunnell; re-analysed by V.-J. Ballester Olmos & M. Borraz Aymerich (FOTOCAT Report #8, 2020)
publisher: academia.edu (174 pp., 102 illus.); print by UPIAR, Turin
taken_from: Viewing area, SW plaque. Bunnell's 2021 rebuttal lists this date as 'Mobile, Mitchell Flat, W', which conflicts with this.
claim: Bunnell: ML with 'combustion pattern'. B&O: probably a vehicle on Nopal Road S-turn
analysability: high - time, bearing, lens known
notes: Ballester Olmos & Borraz found Bunnell's magnetic bearings off by 2.4-3.7 deg (over 800 m at 20 km). Any re-analysis has to correct for this. Both authors are Spain-based, so they are reachable contacts.

title: Bunnell ML1/ML2 series (photos 4-8)
author: James Bunnell / B&O re-analysis
camera: Pentax SLR, 70-300 mm; last 2 frames 35-80 mm
claim: Bunnell: ML at ~44 m altitude, zigzag, crossing a locked gate. B&O: headlights on ranch roads (Nopal/Escondido), bright spots at the gate and S-turns
analysability: high
notes: About 150 deg magnetic is SE of US-67. This is a ranch-road case, not a highway case.

title: Bunnell series (photos 9-13) + Roofus frame
author: James Bunnell / B&O
publisher: as above; Bunnell 2021 'In Defense of the Marfa Lights'
taken_from: Viewing area (Pentax 70-300) and the Roofus automated station at Barlight Ranch (pointing NW)
camera: Pentax SLR 70-300 mm; Roofus low-light monochrome CCD
claim: Bunnell: ML2b crossed Nopal Road without stopping; 'exploding ML' at 80-90 m. B&O: headlights with terrain occlusion
analysability: high (two stations allow triangulation)

title: Bunnell ML2/ML3a/ML3b (photos 14-17)
author: James Bunnell / B&O
claim: Bunnell: 116-124 km/h anomalous lights. B&O: ~55 km/h vehicles on local roads
analysability: high

title: Appendix-3 cases
author: James Bunnell / B&O
date_taken: 2006-08-11; 2006-10-19 (Bunnell: mobile/telescope at the Walnut Creek fault, NW, 'leg-like' heated-air discharges); 2007-07-23
analysability: medium - details are in the PDF appendix, which I didn't read in full

title: Extremely bright luminous object (EBLO)
author: Stephan, Bunnell, Klier, Komala-Noor
time: over 3 h; lightning correlation at 05:30 UTC on 2005-06-03; Bunnell lists photos 00:32-00:52
taken_from: Automated stations Roofus (1) and Snoopy (2), not the viewing area
camera: low-light surveillance cameras, monochrome CCD, star-calibrated photometry
analysability: high scientifically, but outside the viewing-area model; needs station coordinates
notes: The strongest peer-reviewed 'anomalous' case. Test it against your model's road and ranch-light catalogue.
